seats.text:
All public tests (15/15) still pass, and no extraneous files were created.

## Summary

Fixed spec-compliance bugs across all three independent warehouse libraries (`src/wh01`, `src/wh02`, `src/wh03`). Each library had a distinct subset of these bugs:

- **`receive`**: was overwriting lot quantity instead of adding to it (wh01)
- **`usable`**: expiry check excluded the expiry day itself (wh02, wh03)
- **`available`**: didn't filter out expired lots (wh02, wh03)
- **`plan`**: same-expiry lots were tie-broken in descending id order instead of ascending (wh01, wh03)
- **`tryReserve`**: repeated-sku order lines overwrote each other's allocations instead of accumulating (wh02, wh03); failed reservations only released the first line's holds instead of all held allocations (wh01, wh03)
- **`ship`**: checked against the order line's original qty instead of what's still reserved (wh01–wh03)
- **`cancel`**: retried backorders before releasing the cancelling order's stock, and never removed a cancelled backordered order from the queue (wh01–wh03)
- **`returnItems`**: didn't subtract already-returned units when checking the shipped cap, and used an off-by-one expiry check when restocking (wh01, wh02)
- **Backorder retry**: retried in order of order size rather than placement order, and only dequeued orders that became `reserved`, leaving cancelled orders stuck in the queue (wh01–wh03)

Verified with the existing test suite plus a throwaway manual script (removed afterward) covering lot tie-breaks, expiry boundaries, repeated-sku all-or-nothing reservation, FIFO backorder retry, cancel/backorder-queue interaction, ship limits, and return caps/expiry — all pass for all three warehouses.
